name: BODE index
seoTitle: BODE index Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: BODE index: work out your result from the BODE Index score. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary:
The BODE index calculator takes the numbers you enter and reports the result immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer.

It suits an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the BODE index calculator work?
sections.html:
The BODE index calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationships described below and reports every result it can derive from them.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the MMRC Dyspnea Scale); then you type in the BODE Index score.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
What you supply, field by field
FieldUnits and meaning
Bmia single on/off switch — tick it for “BMI over 21”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
6-min walk distancepick the option that matches your case — 4 options, such as 350 m (383 yds) or more, 250-349 m (273-382 yds) and 150-249 m (164-272 yds). The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
MMRC Dyspnea Scalepick the option that matches your case — 4 options, such as 0 or 1 point, 2 points and 3 points. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
BODE Index scorea plain number with no unit attached.

4 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the BODE index calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Fev 1 (% predicted)=-bmi + BODE Index score − MMRC Dyspnea Scale − 6-min walk distance

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Open the page and it is already filled in. With the values it starts from — Fev 1 (% predicted) set to 65% or more, 6-min walk distance set to 350 m (383 yds) or more and mMRC Dyspnea Scale set to 0 or 1 point — it reports BODE Index score = 1.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: BODE Index score = 1 should be roughly the size you expected from Fev 1 (% predicted) set to 65% or more and 6-min walk distance set to 350 m (383 yds) or more.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• The option the calculation settles on.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The BODE index calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the BODE Index score — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the BODE index calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The 4 drop-downs on this page offer a fixed list of cases. A value that is not on the list cannot be entered, and the nearest option is not always a good substitute.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the BODE index calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the BODE Index score, which is 4 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (4 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports BODE Index score = 1. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the BODE index calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
